column2: Same street, two condos. One is freehold, one is leasehold. What changes for you?
Freehold has no end date. Leasehold is a lease from the state, often for ninety-nine years.
When the lease runs out, the land goes back to the state, unless it's renewed.
Renewal isn't automatic. You apply before it ends, and pay a premium the state sets.
Each state has its own rules and rates, so the cost can differ a lot.
Illustration: thirty-five years left on the lease. Some banks may lend less, or for fewer years.
Some titles also need state consent to sell or refinance. That can add weeks, or months.
The upside: leasehold is often priced lower than a similar freehold nearby.
Before you buy, check the title: the tenure, the years left, and any restriction.
Comment title, and we'll check a unit's tenure and years left for you.
